rationale: Approve AS-IS. The candidate recomputes to plan_ref sha256:463bde1c276ddb65b8e0cb0c89ed65a36707a968d75dc744395377f451bd3ba7. Its Amendment-1 delta is confined to §3: Phase B now adds absent cli/ and formally classifies pre-existing connectors/meta-ads-mcp/, whose tracked server.mjs matches DISCOVERY-002 at sha256:df4e115c266ef77441d44eda4785fea1d497e1290165fa136e0bc10fb5a5234f. The A5 whitelist, terminal Phase-B descriptor, final PACKAGE_ROOTS_EXCLUDE classification, Phase-A obligations, AM-42 byte-preservation rule, and every non-§3 obligation remain unchanged. The corrected per-directory deferral is internally consistent: cli/ cannot be classified before it exists, while the existing connector's formal classification must coincide with the single AM-43 activation, package/inventory tightening, and same-PR re-weave rather than splitting that atomic decision. This resolves DISCOVERY-002 without using the erroneous prior wording as authority and preserves the fail-closed two-phase pivot. I explicitly ratify SPIKE-E6-EVALUATOR-FORM and product-1-oq-e6-determinism-deferral because normative oracle enrollment remains blocked until the constrained declarative grammar and trusted evaluator pass their hard merge gate. I also ratify SPIKE-PD001-NOLISTENER-COMPLETENESS and product-1-oq-pd001-nolistener-completeness because the settled kernel-inherited enforcement architecture remains mandatory while only exhaustive residual-corner auditing is deferred behind fail-closed CI observability and slice qualification. The inventory oracle passes on the reviewed state. The broader contract verifier reached 312/313; its sole failure was the review sandbox's read-only /tmp preventing a test fixture from calling mkdtemp, not a repository-contract mismatch or plan defect.
